title: A Crown for the Ember
premise: Ada Delacroix, a beast-speaker concealing a gift outlawed since the Ember War, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Vane, a guild that trades in impossible things. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, Ada discovers his guild has been quietly selling fragments of the old wards to a warlord who means to wake the Ember beneath the mountains. Hunted by guild assassins and shadowed by a wolf who remembers the last war, Ada must choose between destroying the evidence that could save him and carrying it north to reignite an alliance everyone would rather forget. In the end, he spends his secret — and nearly his memory — to relight the wards, buying the world one long winter of grace.
about_author: Isandro Reyes is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing trade ledgers from collapsed merchant houses, an obsession that bleeds into everything he writes. He lives near the coast, where he claims the gulls tell him things he politely declines to repeat.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet Ada balancing the Gilded Vane's books, hiding his beast-speaker gift even from himself, when a caged stormhawk whispers a warning: the wards are thinning. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, the loneliness of a secret kept so long it feels like a scar.

chapters.title: A Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The stars go out mid-audit; the border wards fall in the same hour, and refugees flood the city while the guild quietly raises its prices. Ada overhears Master Corvane selling 'ward-fragments' to a hooded buyer. Emotional beat: vertigo — the world's rules breaking while commerce continues as usual.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A scarred grey wolf speaks to Ada in the refugee crush — not in words but in memories of the last Ember War, including Ada's grandmother's face. It names him heir to something. Emotional beat: terror and longing; for the first time, being seen feels like both salvation and sentence.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Auditing the old ledgers, Ada finds pages in his predecessor's hand recording sales of ward-fragments going back decades — and a note naming the Ember beneath the mountains. Corvane catches him reading. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; knowledge turning from comfort to threat.

chapters.title: The Buyer in Ash-Grey
chapters.summary: Sera Voss POV, introduced. Sera, a ward-smith turned guild enforcer, escorts the ash-grey buyer out of the city and realizes the 'fragments' she's been guarding are alive, humming, grieving. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into guilt; she begins asking questions she was paid not to ask.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Corvane offers Ada partnership and protection in exchange for using his beast-speaker gift to interrogate captured ward-spirits. Refusal means exposure. Ada stalls, stealing a ledger page that night. Emotional beat: moral corrosion beginning; survival offered at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, forced compliance. Ada questions a captive ward-spirit and hears the mountain's Ember stirring, hungry, half-asleep. He lies to Corvane about what it said. Emotional beat: self-disgust braided with resolve; the first deliberate act of rebellion.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Vane
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ordered to hunt a 'ledger thief,' Sera traces the theft to Ada but finds the stolen page proves the guild armed the ward-breakers. She burns her own report instead. Emotional beat: the cost of conscience; choosing a side before meaning to.

chapters.title: Flight Along the Broken Border
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Exposed by a rival clerk, Ada flees with the ledger page and the freed stormhawk, the wolf appearing at his side as guide. Guild hunters follow. Emotional beat: exhilarating, exhausting flight; grief for the life he can never return to.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Sheltering in a village whose residents traded their memories to survive the last winter, Ada meets a woman who doesn't remember her own daughter — and recognizes the price his gift might someday exact. Emotional beat: horror as foreshadowing; memory revealed as currency too.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera intercepts Ada, blade drawn, but instead gives him her ward-smith's sigil and tells him how to reach the northern alliance's last holdfast. She stays behind to mislead the hunters. Emotional beat: sacrifice without absolution; she buys him time she may not survive spending.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Snow falls black with ash; the wolf grows weaker as the land's memory thins. Ada learns the wolf is the last bound guardian of the wards, dying because they fell. Emotional beat: tenderness and urgency entwined; love arriving alongside mortality.

chapters.title: Holdfast of the Unforgiven
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the northern holdfast, descendants of the alliance that ended the Ember War refuse to believe him — until the stormhawk testifies in Ada's voice. Old hatreds flare between factions. Emotional beat: frustration and fragile hope; truth alone convinces no one.

chapters.title: Corvane's Peace
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, captive. Corvane, revealed as the ash-grey buyer's agent, offers the holdfast a deal: surrender Ada and the guild will 'restore' partial wards — powered by feeding the Ember souls. Some lords waver. Emotional beat: seduction of the easy bargain; corruption wearing reasonable clothes.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Before the council, Ada confesses everything: his gift, his years of silence, the ledgers he balanced while the world was sold off. He offers the ledger page and himself. Emotional beat: catharsis through confession; shame transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: March of the Ember-Bound
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Corvane's forces, driving enslaved ward-spirits before them, assault the holdfast as the long winter deepens. Sera escapes her cell and turns the guild's own fragment-cages against them. Emotional beat: chaos and courage; ordinary people choosing at last.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Wakes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Ember breaches the mountain; the sky stays starless and the dead wards scream. The dying wolf carries Ada toward the heart of the old ward-line, asking him to do what his grandmother once refused. Emotional beat: awe and terror at scale; the personal made cosmic.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Ember
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. To relight the wards, someone must wear the crown of living memory and feed it their past. Ada takes it, pouring in his childhood, his mother's voice, his own name — and the wolf gives the last of itself beside him. Emotional beat: transcendence through loss; power accepted only to be given away.

chapters.title: The Ward That Remembers Him
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, aftermath. The wards blaze back to life; the Ember sleeps again; stars return one by one. But Ada remembers almost nothing — the village-woman's fate, now his own. Sera finds him and speaks his name like a key. Emotional beat: hollowed-out peace; identity reduced to what others carry for you.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Gilded Vane falls; Corvane, abandoned by the surviving buyers, faces the rebuilt council. Sera delivers the true ledgers as evidence and refuses a reward, asking instead that impossible things be regulated, not banned. Emotional beat: justice without triumph; systems mended, not avenged.

chapters.title: The Name They Keep for Me
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Living quietly at the holdfast, Ada relearns himself through others' stories — Sera's, the stormhawk's, a journal in his own handwriting. The gift survives, quieter now; beasts still speak to him gently. Emotional beat: tentative reclamation; a self rebuilt from borrowed light.

chapters.title: First Stars Over the Pass
chapters.summary: Ada and Sera's shared POV, closing chapter. On the first clear night, Ada and Sera climb the pass where the wolf fell and watch the constellations return. Ada plants a crown-shaped stone there. Somewhere below, a child laughs at a talking bird. Emotional beat: earned grace; memory kept alive by being shared, the long winter ending not with victory but with vigilance.
